answer: Each identity holds one 100-credit anchor position in its island tide market, key-bound, never merged. Each tide cycle charges every position a fixed 15-credit fee. Auditors recompute positions and fees from the island ledger; any merged, shared, or copied position is closed and burned. The k-th fake still locks 100 and pays 15 per cycle, so 1,000 fakes lock 100,000 and pay 15,000 per cycle. Position rental fails: the rented position carries the owner's key, so the renter cannot withdraw it. An honest identity holds one anchor position, pays 15 per cycle, and recovers 100 on exit.
